finding.claim: pool.escape() falls back to backslash escape mode when no idle connection exists, so under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES the escaped output is injectable
finding.source: Attacker-controlled input passed to pool.escape(value) by the application, with the server in NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES sql_mode and no idle pooled connection at call time
finding.sink: String returned by pool.escape() spliced into SQL as a string literal (lib/pool.js:677-678 via lib/misc/utils.js:253-257)

trace.note: escape(value) calls Utils.escape(opts, this._searchInfo(), value)
_searchInfo returns idle connection info when one exists (correct path)
with no idle connection, for...in over Object.keys yields indices '0'..'n-1'
indices looked up in #activeConnections, which is keyed by server threadId (see lib/pool.js:493, :560), so lookup returns undefined
undefined conn triggers break; conn stays null
info remains null
info != null is false, so noBackslashEscapes is false and the backslash escape table is used
input ' OR 1=1 -- escapes to '\' OR 1=1 -- ' which under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES closes the literal early and leaves injected SQL live

finding.guards_checked: Idle-connection path is correct (pool.js:527). Connection.escape uses the connection's own info (connection.js:112), so it is unaffected. escapeId is mode-independent (backtick doubling, utils.js:97-113). Placeholder formatting goes through the connection and is unaffected. Only pool-level escape with no idle connection is affected. Not executed; verified by reading.

finding.claim: LOCAL INFILE filename validation is case-insensitive, so a malicious server can request a case-variant of the app-named file and the client opens the server-chosen path
finding.source: Malicious or compromised server sends a LOCAL INFILE request; app has enabled permitLocalInfile and its query names a file

trace.note: permitLocalInfile gate (default false, connection-options.js:158-167)
Parse.validateFileName(sql, initialValues, fileName) called with server fileName
regex metacharacters in fileName are escaped correctly
RegExp built with 'i' flag, so match against SQL literal is case-insensitive
placeholder branch compares with toLowerCase(), also case-insensitive
file opened using server-supplied fileName, not the SQL literal

finding.guards_checked: permitLocalInfile default off and enforced (parser.js:742). Regex metacharacter escaping (parse.js:408). Closing-quote anchor requires exact-length match. Narrow impact: only case variants of the app-named file are reachable and only matter on case-sensitive filesystems where a variant exists.

finding.claim: A server-directed redirect opens a new connection to a server-chosen host using the app's configured password, so credentials are disclosed to that host
finding.source: Database server (or a compromised server) sends a mariadb:// or mysql:// redirect string
finding.sink: New Connection built from this.opts including the password (lib/connection.js:2111-2112)

trace.note: redirect only when opts.permitRedirect
permitRedirect defaults on only when ssl is set and rejectUnauthorized !== false
target host and port parsed from server-supplied URL
same-host short-circuit
user and password override only if present in URL
new connection built from this.opts, retaining the app password

finding.guards_checked: permitRedirect default requires TLS with certificate verification. Redirect skipped inside transactions (connection.js:2076). Same-host short-circuit. Exposure requires a compromised DB server or a publicly trusted host controlled by the attacker, so this is a trust-boundary issue rated low.

finding.claim: sha256_password public-key retrieval over a non-TLS connection lets the server supply the RSA key the password is encrypted under, disclosing the password to an attacker who controls the connection
finding.source: Attacker controls the network path or the server, and the app sets allowPublicKeyRetrieval without TLS
finding.sink: Password RSA-encrypted under a server-supplied key (sha256-password-auth.js:86-87)

trace.note: no rsaPublicKey configured, so the client path is used
refused unless allowPublicKeyRetrieval is set
client requests key from server on opt-in
password encrypted under server-supplied key

finding.guards_checked: Explicit opt-in required (allowPublicKeyRetrieval) and error thrown otherwise (:61-70). Documented protocol property; low severity, opt-in only.
